title: Chicken in a sour onion and vinegar sauce
desc: A sour onion-and-vinegar sauce, traditionally served with kidneys, here on chicken thighs. Green beans on the side.
trouble: One more spoon of cream, bubble 30 seconds.
Lower the heat and add a splash of the stock.

steps.t: Put the green beans on in salted boiling water for 7 minutes, then drain.
steps.c: Bright green, still a little bite.
steps.img: green beans boiling in a small pot

steps.t: Brown the chicken in half the butter on high heat for 6 minutes, then take it out. Add the rest of the butter and the onions and fry 6 minutes on medium until golden.
steps.w: Golden onions give the dark base of a sour-kidney sauce.
steps.c: Chicken browned at the edges, onions soft and golden.
steps.m: Pale onions: the sauce stays thin and sharp.
steps.img: thinly sliced onions softly fried until golden brown in butter in a heavy pan, loose soft onion strips, not battered, not onion rings

steps.t: Make the sauce: dust the onions with the flour, stir 30 seconds, pour in the stock, vinegar, mustard and bay leaf, scrape up the brown bits and bubble 3 minutes until it coats a spoon. Stir in the cream and the chicken, warm 2 minutes, season and scatter parsley.
steps.w: Vinegar against browned onions and a little cream: that is the classic sour-kidney taste.
steps.c: Glossy brown sauce that coats the back of a spoon.
steps.m: Boiling hard after the cream: it can split.
steps.img: chicken strips in a glossy brown sour onion sauce

title: Meatballs in a lemon-caper cream sauce
desc: A classic: soft meatballs simmered in stock, then a white sauce sharpened with lemon and capers. Broccoli on the side.
trouble: Barely simmer them; a rolling boil breaks them.
Whisk the stock in a little at a time.

steps.t: Mix the mince with the egg, breadcrumbs, grated onion, salt and pepper. Roll 10 balls.
steps.c: Smooth balls that hold their shape.
steps.img: ten raw meatballs on a board

steps.t: Bring the stock to a bare simmer, add the meatballs and poach 12 minutes. Steam the broccoli over it or in a second pot for the last 6 minutes. Lift out the meatballs, keep 400 ml of the stock.
steps.w: Poaching keeps them soft; the stock becomes the sauce.
steps.img: meatballs poaching in a pot of stock

steps.t: Make the sauce: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the 400 ml stock bit by bit and simmer 3 minutes until it coats a spoon. Stir in the cream, capers and lemon juice, put the meatballs back for 2 minutes and scatter parsley.
steps.w: Lemon and capers make the white sauce sour; that is the point of the dish.
steps.c: Smooth, pale sauce that coats the back of a spoon.
steps.m: All the stock at once: lumps.
steps.img: meatballs in a pale lemon caper cream sauce

title: Beef patties in a sour spiced gravy
desc: The sour, spiced gravy of a slow Sunday pot roast (vinegar, bay, cloves, allspice), on quick beef patties. No sugar, no raisins. Carrots on the side.
trouble: Bubble one more minute, or a pinch more corn flour mixed in water.
Don't press them down in the pan.
goes: Carrots; red cabbage if you have it.

steps.t: Boil the carrots in salted water for 12 minutes, then drain.
steps.img: sliced carrots in a pot

steps.t: Mix the mince with the egg, the grated half of the onion, salt and pepper; shape 4 patties. Fry them in the oil 4 minutes a side on medium-high, then take them out.
steps.m: Turning too early: they stick and tear.
steps.img: four round beef mince patties browning in a frying pan, only the patties in the pan, no egg

steps.t: Make the sauce in the patty pan: fry the sliced onion and tomato paste 2 minutes, pour in the stock and vinegar, add bay, cloves and allspice, scrape up the brown bits and bubble 3 minutes. Stir in the corn flour and bubble 1 minute until it coats a spoon. Put the patties back for 2 minutes.
steps.w: Vinegar plus clove and allspice is the pot-roast taste, without marinating for days.
steps.c: Dark, glossy, coats the back of a spoon.
steps.m: Leaving the cloves in to serve: fish them out.
steps.img: patties in a dark glossy gravy in a pan

title: Steak with crispy onions and a sour onion gravy
desc: Steak with a heap of crisp-edged onions and a short, sharp gravy from the pan, the classic way. Carrots on the side. Counts as red meat.
trouble: Pan hotter and dry the steak first.
Fry them in batches, don't crowd the pan.

steps.t: Boil the carrot sticks in salted water 10 minutes. Dust the onion rings with the flour and fry them in the butter on medium 8 minutes until golden; take them out.
steps.img: a heavy pan of thinly sliced onions fried golden with crisp brown edges, loose soft onion strips, not battered, not onion rings, a pot of carrot sticks beside it

steps.t: Salt the steaks and fry in the oil on high heat 3 minutes a side, then rest them 3 minutes on a plate.
steps.w: Resting keeps the juice in the meat.
steps.m: Cutting straight away: the juice runs out.
steps.img: two steaks searing in a hot pan

steps.t: Make the sauce in the steak pan: pour in the stock, vinegar and mustard, scrape up the brown bits and bubble 2 minutes until it coats a spoon. Pour it over the steaks and pile the onions on top.
steps.w: The steak crust in the pan is the flavour of the gravy.
steps.img: steak topped with a heap of fried onions and gravy

title: Pollo all'aceto: chicken thighs in garlic-vinegar sauce
desc: An Italian home dish: chicken thighs browned, then glazed with red-wine vinegar, garlic and rosemary. Sharp and quick. Broccoli on the side.
trouble: Bubble 1 minute longer: the vinegar mellows.
Add it after the chicken has browned, not before.

steps.t: Steam or boil the broccoli 5 minutes and drain.
steps.img: broccoli florets in a pot

steps.t: Salt the chicken and brown it skin- or smooth-side down in the oil on medium-high 7 minutes, turn and cook 5 more. Add the garlic and rosemary for the last 2 minutes.
steps.m: Garlic in too early: it burns.
steps.img: chicken thighs browning with sliced garlic and rosemary

steps.t: Make the sauce: pour in the vinegar and stock, scrape up the brown bits and bubble 3 minutes, turning the chicken, until it is glossy and coats a spoon. Swirl in the butter.
steps.w: The vinegar cooks down into a sharp glaze around the chicken.
steps.m: Taking it off too early: harsh and thin.
steps.img: chicken thighs glazed in a glossy vinegar sauce

title: Pork medallions in mustard-vinegar cream, with broccoli
desc: Pork tenderloin medallions in a sharp mustard cream with a dash of vinegar. 25 minutes. Counts as red meat.
trouble: Medallions need only 3 minutes a side.
Keep it at a gentle bubble after the cream.

steps.t: Steam or boil the broccoli 5 minutes and drain.
steps.img: broccoli florets in a pot

steps.t: Salt the pork medallions and fry them in the butter on medium-high 3 minutes a side; put them on a plate.
steps.c: Golden both sides, just pink inside.
steps.m: Crowding the pan: they steam grey.
steps.img: pork medallions browning in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce in the pork pan: soften the shallot 1 minute, add the vinegar and stock and scrape up the brown bits, stir in the mustard and cream and bubble 2 minutes until it coats a spoon. Return the pork and its juices for 1 minute.
steps.c: Pale, glossy, coats the back of a spoon.
steps.img: pork medallions in a creamy mustard sauce

left: Keeps a day in the fridge; it gets better.
title: Chicken and cheese salad with onion in a sharp dressing
desc: A sausage-salad-style dish made with leftover chicken instead of sausage: strips of chicken and cheese, onion rings, a sharp vinegar dressing. No cooking, 8 minutes.

steps.t: Put the chicken, Emmental, onion rings and pepper strips in a bowl.
steps.img: a large glass salad bowl on a kitchen table holding strips of cooked chicken, strips of yellow Emmental cheese, thin red onion rings and red pepper strips, no pan, no stove

steps.t: Make the sauce for this salad: whisk the vinegar, oil, mustard, salt and pepper with a fork for 30 seconds until cloudy, pour over, toss and leave 2 minutes. Scatter the spring onion.
steps.w: A salad like this lives on a sharp dressing.
steps.m: Too little vinegar: it tastes flat.
steps.img: a fork whisking a vinegar and oil dressing in a small glass bowl next to a salad bowl of chicken and cheese strips, no pan, no stove

title: Mince and broccoli pan with a mustard-vinegar glaze
desc: Twelve minutes, one pan: browned beef mince and small broccoli florets in a short mustard-vinegar glaze.
trouble: Hotter pan, don't stir for the first 2 minutes.

steps.t: Brown the mince with the onion in the oil on high heat 5 minutes. Add the broccoli, garlic, paprika and 2 tbsp of the water, lid on, 4 minutes.
steps.w: The lid steams the broccoli in the same pan.
steps.img: mince and broccoli florets in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: stir in the mustard, vinegar and the last spoon of water, scrape the pan and bubble 1 minute until glossy and it coats the mince. Season.
steps.c: Shiny, nothing watery in the pan.
steps.img: glossy mince and broccoli in a pan

left: Keeps a day in the fridge.
title: Sliced beef salad in a sharp vinegar dressing
desc: Beef salad: thin slices of leftover steak with red onion, pepper and chives in a sour vinegar dressing. No cooking with leftovers, 8 minutes. Counts as red meat.
trouble: Slice it thin, across the grain.

steps.t: Slice the beef thinly across the grain and put it in a bowl with the onion rings and pepper strips.
steps.img: thin slices of cooked pink beef with red onion rings and red pepper strips in a large glass salad bowl on a kitchen table, no pan, no stove

steps.t: Make the sauce for this salad: whisk the vinegar, oil, mustard, salt and pepper with a fork for 30 seconds until cloudy, pour it over the beef and toss. Serve on the lettuce with the spring onion.
steps.img: beef salad with a vinegar dressing served on lettuce leaves on a plate, no pan, no stove

title: Paprika chicken bowl with tomatoes and quick-pickled onion
desc: Thin chicken strips fried in 6 minutes, over lettuce with tomatoes and pepper, and red onion pickled in vinegar while the chicken cooks. 12 minutes.
trouble: Leave it in the vinegar the full 5 minutes.

steps.t: Put the onion rings in the vinegar with a pinch of salt and leave them. Toss the chicken with paprika and salt and fry in the oil on high heat 6 minutes.
steps.w: Five minutes in vinegar turns the onion pink and mild.
steps.img: paprika chicken strips frying next to a bowl of pink pickled onion

steps.t: Make the sauce: tip the tomatoes into the hot pan for 1 minute, press them with a fork, add 1 tbsp of the onion vinegar and scrape until it bubbles and coats the chicken. Pile it on the lettuce and pepper, top with the pickled onion and parsley.
steps.img: chicken bowl with tomatoes lettuce and pickled red onion

title: Scrambled eggs with pancetta and onion
desc: A slow Sunday breakfast: crisp pancetta and soft onion, folded into creamy scrambled eggs. Ten minutes.
trouble: Take them off the heat while still wet.

steps.t: Fry the pancetta in a dry pan on medium 4 minutes until crisp, add the onion and the butter and soften 2 minutes.
steps.img: crisp diced pancetta and onion in a pan

steps.t: Turn the heat to low, pour in the eggs and stir slowly 2–3 minutes until soft curds form. Off the heat, scatter spring onion and pepper.
steps.w: Low heat gives soft, creamy eggs.
steps.img: creamy scrambled eggs with pancetta and onion

title: Weekend beef goulash with a sour paprika finish (6 portions, freezes)
desc: A weekend pot: beef chunks braised slowly with lots of onion and paprika, finished with a dash of vinegar. Six portions: eat two, freeze four for weekday dinners. Counts as red meat.
reheat: From frozen: thaw overnight, warm 10 minutes in a pan.
trouble: Another 20 minutes, lid on, low heat.
Take the pot off the heat before stirring it in.
goes: Broccoli or green beans; potatoes or rice.

steps.t: Brown the beef in the oil in two batches on high heat, 5 minutes each, and set aside. Fry the onions in the same pot 10 minutes on medium until soft and golden, add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
steps.w: Browning in batches gives colour; crowding steams the meat grey.
steps.m: All the meat at once: it stews instead of browning.
steps.img: beef chunks browning in a large pot

steps.t: Take the pot off the heat, stir in both paprikas, then add the stock, bay leaves and beef. Lid on, lowest heat, 75 minutes; add the pepper chunks for the last 20.
steps.w: Paprika burns in seconds on direct heat.
steps.c: Meat falls apart under a fork.
steps.m: Paprika on the hot pan: bitter.
steps.img: goulash simmering in a large pot

steps.t: Make the sauce: lid off, stir in the vinegar, salt and pepper and bubble 10 minutes until it thickens and coats a spoon. Eat two portions, cool the rest and freeze in four single boxes.
steps.w: The vinegar at the end gives the sour finish you like.
steps.c: Thick, glossy, coats the back of a spoon.
steps.m: Freezing it hot: let it cool first.
steps.img: thick red goulash in a pot with a ladle
